context:
Use the existing Python comparator unchanged. Each integration test
builds (reference_rows, comparison_rows) via each platform's existing
adapter, then calls compare_query_results() and asserts report.matched.

For ClickHouse-local, lean on the existing docker harness in
docker/clickhouse/. For Polars-DF and DataFusion, reuse the dataframe
platform runners directly.

Start with TPC-H SF=0.01 only. Expand to TPC-DS as a separate follow-up
once TPC-H is stable in nightly for at least one week.
description:
Follow-up slice of quality-add-cross-platform-result-validation.

That TODO delivered the comparator (benchbox/core/validation/cross_platform.py),
its unit tests (tests/unit/core/test_cross_platform_validation.py), and
the developer doc (docs/development/result-validation.md). What remains is
the live integration matrix and the nightly workflow - both require
platform credentials or heavier local infrastructure, so they were split
off to preserve bounded review surface.

Scope:
  - Integration pytest suite at tests/integration/validation/test_cross_platform.py
    that executes the standard query sets on DuckDB (reference) vs each
    comparison platform at SF=0.01.
  - First matrix stays credential-free: DuckDB × {DataFusion, Polars-DF,
    ClickHouse-local container}. Cloud platforms (Snowflake, Databricks)
    are a separate follow-up if/when the nightly lane gains secrets.
  - Nightly workflow at .github/workflows/cross-platform-validation.yml
    running the suite and publishing structured diff artifacts on failure.

anti_patterns.instead: file a new comparator TODO if behavior needs to change
anti_patterns.why: the unit suite pins its contract

anti_patterns.instead: snowflake/databricks join in a separate slice
anti_patterns.why: the first matrix is credential-free by design

anti_patterns.dont: paper over a divergence with loose tolerance
anti_patterns.instead: every loosened Tolerance must cite a spec rule in the rationale field

anti_patterns.dont: run the suite on every PR
anti_patterns.why: cross-platform suites are expensive and flaky under cloud noise

preserves.behavior: Comparator module (benchbox/core/validation/cross_platform.py) untouched by this TODO - it is already shipped
Fast test lane duration unchanged - new tests are live_integration only
No new required PR check - nightly-only signal; CI on PR stays as-is

verifications.description: Integration suite passes locally on the no-credentials matrix
New integration test file carries no mark.fast markers - fast lane unaffected

work_units.summary: Write tests/integration/validation/test_cross_platform.py: DuckDB × DataFusion, TPC-H SF=0.01; comparator STRICT by default; Tolerance overrides must cite spec rules
Extend the suite to DuckDB × Polars-DF and DuckDB × ClickHouse-local (docker). Keep test markers = live_integration so the fast lane is unaffected.
Add .github/workflows/cross-platform-validation.yml running on cron (nightly) plus workflow_dispatch. On failure, upload a structured JSON diff artifact per failed (benchmark, platform-pair) cell.
Document a triage runbook: how to read the diff artifact, how to file a TODO with spec-anchored rationale if the divergence is legitimate, and how to roll back an adapter change that broke a column.
